Rows 2-8 form a uniform white header band with a centred green cross emblem, which makes it a vertical sign or header panel rather than a horizontal surface. It has a darker line at row 9 and a shadow at row 10, but no foreshortened top plane, no ellipse and no roof plane. Rows 11-23 are glass-door compartments with boxes shown face-on, not contents seen from above. Rows 24-28 are drawer fronts. The silhouette is a constant 30 px wide from row 0 to row 31, with no receding side face. It has no opening seen from above, so it is not a container with an opening.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine for density: 18 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, and 0% near-flat coverage. The structure is where it falls short. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the cabinet has a uniform grey-black outline around the body and doors. That is the sticker look, not the tinted, material-toned edges of the hedge (0% neutral), the stall (1%) or the well (33%). The pale cabinet body and door frames read as roughly 3-4 lightness steps (white, light grey, mid grey, outline) against 5-6 on the reference materials. The glass doors and shelf items give some detail, but there is little grain or speckle on the large white panels. Only the shelf contents and the cross add variety, so the piece sits a little below the references in craft.
